subject: ela
intro: Students learn to distinguish fiction stories from informational books and to recognize key features of poems (rhyme, rhythm, short lines) versus stories (characters, setting, plot). This skill builds awareness that different types of texts are organized and written for different purposes.

items.prompt:
Read this text below.

Mia the frog hopped to the big pond. She met a turtle named Ted. 'Come swim with me!' she said. They splashed and played all afternoon.

Is this text a fiction story, an informational book, or a poem? How do you know?

steps: I ask: are there made-up characters in a made-up story? Yes, Mia the frog and Ted the turtle are made-up characters who talk.
Does it have a setting, characters, and events? Yes: a pond, two characters, and a sequence of events.
Is it trying to teach me real facts? No, frogs and turtles do not really talk.
So this is a fiction story.
solution.answer: This is a fiction story. It has made-up characters (Mia the frog and Ted the turtle), a setting (the pond), and events (swimming and playing). The animals talk, which does not happen in real life.

items.prompt:
Read this text below.

Frogs are amphibians. They can live in water and on land. Frogs lay their eggs in water. Tadpoles hatch from the eggs and slowly grow legs.

Is this text a fiction story, an informational book, or a poem? How do you know?

steps: Are there characters in a made-up story? No, there are no characters named or doing things.
Is it giving real facts? Yes: facts about frogs, their eggs, and their life cycle.
Does it try to teach something true about the real world? Yes.
So this is an informational text.
solution.answer: This is an informational text. It gives real facts about frogs, such as that they are amphibians and how they grow from tadpoles. It does not have characters or a made-up story.

items.prompt:
Read this text below.

The sun is warm upon my face,
I run and play in every place.
The grass is soft beneath my feet,
And summer days are oh so sweet!

Is this text a fiction story, an informational book, or a poem? How do you know?

steps: Do I see rhymes? Yes: face/place, feet/sweet.
Are the lines short, like a poem? Yes.
Does it tell a story with a plot? No.
Does it give facts? No.
So this is a poem.
solution.answer: This is a poem. It has rhyming words (face/place, feet/sweet) and short lines. It does not tell a story with a problem and solution, and it does not give facts about the world.

items.prompt: What are two ways a fiction story is different from an informational book?

steps: I think about what I know about each type.
Fiction: has made-up characters, a made-up setting, and a plot. Events may not be real.
Informational: has real facts. The purpose is to teach something true.
Difference 1: Fiction has characters doing things in a story. Informational books have facts and information.
Difference 2: Fiction may have things that could not happen in real life. Informational books only include real information.
solution.answer: First, fiction stories have made-up characters in a made-up plot, while informational books give real facts. Second, fiction can include events that do not happen in real life (like talking animals), while informational texts only describe real things.

items.prompt:
Read this text below.

Bears sleep all winter long,
In caves so dark and cold.
They wake up in the spring, you know,
When days grow warm and bold.

A student said this is an informational text because it talks about bears. Do you agree or disagree? Explain.

steps: I check: does it have rhymes? Yes, long/bold and cold/bold rhyme.
Are the lines short and arranged like a poem? Yes.
Even though it mentions real facts about bears, the way it is written (rhyming lines) makes it a poem.
Informational texts are usually written in paragraphs with plain sentences.
So I disagree. It is a poem about bears, not an informational text.
solution.answer: I disagree. Even though it mentions real facts about bears, it is written as a poem. It has rhyming lines and short stanzas, which are features of poetry. Informational texts are usually written in plain paragraphs, not rhyming lines.

items.prompt:
Read this text below.

The moon glows silver in the night,
A pale and quiet, gentle light.
It watches over every dream,
And things are never what they seem.

Is this a poem, a fiction story, or an informational book? Give two reasons.
items.hint: Look for rhymes and short lines. Ask: does it have characters and a plot? Does it give real facts?

steps: Rhymes: night/light, dream/seem.
Short lines arranged in a regular pattern.
No characters, no plot, no real facts being taught.
It is a poem.
solution.answer: This is a poem. First, it has rhyming words (night/light and dream/seem). Second, it is written in short lines arranged in stanzas, not paragraphs. It does not have characters or give real facts about the moon.

items.prompt:
Read this text below.

Birds have feathers, wings, and beaks. Most birds can fly, but some cannot. Penguins are birds that swim instead of fly. There are more than 10,000 kinds of birds in the world.

Is this a poem, a fiction story, or an informational text? Give two reasons.
items.hint: Ask: are there characters? Is there a plot? Does it give real facts?

steps: Are there characters in a story? No.
Is it giving real facts? Yes: feathers, wings, penguins, 10,000 kinds.
Is it written in rhyming lines? No.
It is an informational text.
solution.answer: This is an informational text. First, it gives real facts about birds, like that penguins cannot fly and there are over 10,000 kinds. Second, it has no characters or plot. It is written in plain sentences meant to teach facts.

items.prompt:
Read this text below.

Leo the lion was sad. His mane had gone flat in the rain. He sat by a puddle and sighed. Just then, a little bird flew over and sang him a sunny song. Leo smiled.

Is this a fiction story or an informational text? How do you know?
items.hint: Look for made-up characters, a problem, and a solution.

steps: Are there made-up characters? Yes: Leo the lion and a little bird.
Is there a problem? Yes: Leo is sad because his mane went flat.
Is there a solution? Yes: the bird's song cheered him up.
Does it give real facts? No.
It is a fiction story.
solution.answer: This is a fiction story. It has made-up characters (Leo the lion and a bird), a problem (Leo was sad), and a solution (the bird's song). It does not give real facts about lions.

items.prompt: A friend says: 'Poems are always short, so any short text is a poem.' Is your friend correct? Explain using what you know about different text types.
items.hint: Think about what makes something a poem vs. a short story or a short fact.

steps: Poems are often short, but not all short texts are poems.
A short story still has characters, a setting, and events.
A short informational text can give facts in just two sentences.
What makes something a poem is rhyme, rhythm, or the way lines are arranged, not length.
solution.answer: My friend is not quite right. Poems can be short, but not everything short is a poem. A short text might still be a story (with characters and events) or a fact (telling you something real). What makes a poem a poem is its use of rhyme, rhythm, or the way it arranges words in lines, not how many words it has.

items.prompt:
Read this text below.

Volcanoes are mountains that can erupt. When they erupt, hot melted rock called lava pours out. Some volcanoes are under the ocean. Scientists called volcanologists study them.

And read this text below.

Deep in the earth, the fire dragon slept. One day he sneezed. Hot red tears rolled down the mountain. The whole valley shook with his mighty yawn.

Which text is informational and which is fiction? How are they different?
items.hint: Check for real facts in one and a made-up story in the other.

steps: First text: gives real facts about volcanoes, lava, and volcanologists. No characters. Informational.
Second text: has a made-up fire dragon that causes the volcano. That is a story, not real facts.
Both are about volcanoes, but one teaches real information and one tells a made-up story.
solution.answer: The first text is informational. It gives real facts about volcanoes, like what lava is and who studies them. The second text is fiction. It has a made-up character (a fire dragon) and a made-up story. Both are about volcanoes, but the informational text teaches facts while the fiction story makes up a creative explanation.
